generic_name: Desogestrel and Ethinyl Estradiol / Ethinyl Estradiol
drug_class: Combination Hormonal Contraceptive (Triphasic Oral Contraceptive Pill)
purpose: This medication is a birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help regulate your menstrual cycle, reduce painful periods, or treat acne in some cases. It contains two hormones — a progestin called desogestrel and an estrogen called ethinyl estradiol — that work together to prevent pregnancy.
how_it_works: This pill works in three main ways to prevent pregnancy. First, it stops your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. Second, it thickens the mucus in your cervix, making it harder for sperm to reach an egg. Third, it changes the lining of your uterus so that a fertilized egg is less likely to attach and grow. The 'triphasic' part means the hormone doses change slightly across three phases of your pill pack, mimicking your natural cycle.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, headaches, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods (especially in the first few months), mood changes, decreased sex drive, and bloating. These often improve after the first 2-3 months as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do not smoke while taking this medication, especially if you are over 35 years old — it significantly raises your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. Stop taking the pill and contact your doctor right away if you experience severe chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, leg pain or swelling, severe headache, vision changes, or yellowing of the skin or eyes. This pill does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers.
typical_dosing: You take one pill by mouth every day at the same time each day. The pill pack has 28 pills total — 21 active hormone pills (in three color-coded groups with slightly different hormone levels) and 7 inactive reminder pills. You take the reminder pills during your period week. Start your first pack as directed by your doctor — either on the first day of your period or on the first Sunday after your period starts. Try to take it at the same time every day to get the best protection and to reduce nausea.
